#38223 This is the first in a series of PRs towards the categorical construction of smooth functors on finite-dimensional vector spaces. For more details on the background and motivation, see #Is there code for X? > Category Theory: Smooth Functors. The file structure is heavily based on Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Basic.lean. I will make additional PRs soon showing that this category is monoidal and enriches FGModuleCat--the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces.

I am still new to doing category theory in lean, so anyone who is familiar with that part of the codebase I would really appreciate a review! :-)
This topic was moved here from #PR reviews > #38223 The Category of C^n Manifolds by Jack McCarthy.

Jack McCarthy said:

I am still new to doing category theory in lean, so anyone who is familiar with that part of the codebase I would really appreciate a review! :-)

I will take a look next week, Thursday at the latest.

Further Info for Reviewer

This file copies Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Basic.lean exactly with the following changes:

  1. Replaced Continuous↦ ContMDiff, Homeomorph ↦ Diffeomorph, etc.
  2. Replaced [TopologicalSpace X] with the manifold assumptions : [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace H] [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I n M]
  3. Category MfldCat depends on parameters 𝕜 (a field) and n (smoothness parameter)
  4. Updated: All fields of MfldCat live in separate universes. Requires @[nolint checkUnivs]. Objects M in MfldCat carry model data E H I, all living in Type u.
  5. imported: Geometry/Manifold/Diffeomorph (based on #min_imports)
  6. Rewrote module docstring.
  7. Removed Discrete and Trivial functors -- AFAIK there is no discrete/trivial smooth structure on a generic Type u. Unclear. (line 178 in TopCat)
  8. Removed isOpenMap/isClosedMap isomorphism theorems -- These don't hold in the smooth case. (line 226 in TopCat)
  9. Added ofNormedSpace -- i.e. "A normed space is a C^n manfiold"
  10. Added forgetful functor MfldCat ⥤ TopCat -- i.e. "A smooth manifold is a topological space"
  11. Added TODO: Define a functor FGModuleCat 𝕜 ⥤ MfldCat 𝕜 n (future work)

(This list was compiled by a human. Coding session was human-driven, Claude-assisted.)
As an aside, whenever I see forgetful I wonder what the free is and of course there isn't one in this case.

I am a bit unclear in the above description as to where k fits in in this universe design decision.

In practice k will be R\RR or C\mathbb{C}C and these are in Type. Are you then committing to having the entire set-up in Type in this case?

As a mathematician this doesn't bother me, I think universes are overrated other than in very specific parts of the library corresponding to where there are set-theoretic subtleties in the underlying mathematics eg etale cohomology. But it might bother some people here who argue that we should be maximally using the universe system.
Yes, you make very good point -- 𝕜 and M could live in different universes. We can compare to ModuleCat where an R-module lives in a separate universe than R itself.

Updated-- 𝕜 : Type v and everything else is Type u. I'm still think it would be best to keep carrier, E, H and I in the same universe, but I will try to work on a generalized version where they are all Type*

Update 2-- MfldCat is now fully polymorphic! All data live in separate universes.
cc @Ben Eltschig who is working on related things.

Update 3 -- Uh oh, it appears I should not have been so zealous in making everything universe polymorphic. I am now getting a "BAD UNIVERSE LEVELS" warning from the checkUnivs linter, and my CI build is failing. I will need to do some more studying on the universe system.
sometimes in bundled structures with multiple universe variables the "BAD UNIVERSE LEVELS" warning is wrong, see for example docs#PFunctor

Yes, I can add @[nolint checkUnivs] (like in PFunctor) but I'm not sure I could really defend why that is a good design choice here. The ChartedSpace gives us charts M → H, and the ModelWithCorners gives us a PartialEquiv E H. So IMO, it makes sense for M, H, E to all live in Type u (which avoids the nolint). I'd love to get a second opinion on this.

I will add the nolint for now, but it seems like a lot of complexity for a generalization which will never be used in practice. I agree with Kevin's take here: universes are overrated!

after looking at the PR, I can confirm that adding @[nolint checkUnivs] is indeed the correct thing to do here, since checkUnivs only looks at the type of the definition it misses the fact that u₂ and u₃ and u₄ appear by themselves in the body

("Diff" here denotes the category MfldCat ℝ ∞, my construction is of course more general)

My only point about universes was that I thought k should be allowed to be in a different universe to everything else (because we don't have a good theory of polymorphic reals). I didn't object to everything else being in the same universe.

cc Ben Eltschig who is working on related things.

Right, sorry - I already have code for this category here and code for the subcategory of finite-dimensional manifolds here, I just procrastinated PRing it because there were some design choices I was still not 100% confident about (mainly making FinDimMfld a docs#CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`). I'm sorry that this has resulted in some duplication of work, but I'm happy to review your PRs and hope we can coordinate future ones.

Jack McCarthy said:

Yes, I can add @[nolint checkUnivs] (like in PFunctor) but I'm not sure I could really defend why that is a good design choice here. The ChartedSpace gives us charts M → H, and the ModelWithCorners gives us a PartialEquiv E H. So IMO, it makes sense for M, H, E to all live in Type u (which avoids the nolint). I'd love to get a second opinion on this.

Having everything but the ground field live in the same universe is also what I went with - I don't think there's any examples of large manifolds modelled on small spaces that we care about, and if we run into one we can still always get the universe levels to align using docs#ULift and docs#Shrink

(mathematically, if I'm seeing things correctly every connected manifold has to fit in the same universe as the space it is modelled on, so the only manifolds living in strictly higher universes are disjoint unions of small manifolds - of course we could still run into situations where a connected small manifold lives in a higher universe than its model space for technical reasons, but I don't think that is worth worrying about much)

Hi Ben! I just took a look at your diffeology code. It very deep, you clearly are much more versed in categorical differential geometry. I am also not 100% confident about all of my design choices (as demonstrated by the universe discussion above), but hopefully together we can come to something that is idiomatic for Mathlib. Thanks for leaving a review on my PR!

Ben Eltschig said:

Having everything but the ground field live in the same universe is also what I went with - I don't think there's any examples of large manifolds modelled on small spaces that we care about, and if we run into one we can still always get the universe levels to align using docs#ULift and docs#Shrink

Thanks for confirming that I've not completely lost my mind. I agree, we should never care about large manifolds modelled on small spaces. But I didn't want to force that into Mathlib in case there is someone out there who wants such functionality. You make a good argument about Ulift and Shrink, I'm going to revert back to the two-universe model like in your repo.

I don't think it's unreasonable to simply ask the community (e.g. in #mathlib4 ) whether this might be the case. In algebra there really are some times when you want to be a little careful to allow general universes, for example sometimes (e.g. in one of the definitions of etale cohomology) it's convenient to take a limit over something which in ZFC would not be a set, giving you a limit object which in Lean ends up in one universe higher than the things you started with, and then perhaps later on you descend the object back down (perhaps after proving some things about it). However sometimes we are lazy about universes and then suddenly it bites us: for example there was a point where we could not take group cohomology of something which wasn't in Type because someone hard baked a Z\ZZ into something and then someone else hard baked equality of two universes into something else and all of a sudden everything had to be in Type, and this was not really ideal. This was why I flagged the issue about Real : Type -- I was concerned that the same thing might happen here. However it might simply not be important. For example If some design decision two years ago meant that now all real manifolds had to be in Type then I would be very confident that this would not be any trouble at all in the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem (which certainly needs manifolds). However if there were limitations on universes in algebraic geometry I would be a bit more worried. This is why you might want to speak to the experts.

update-- I've responded to the initial round of comments by @Ben Eltschig @Christian Merten. Thanks for all of the great input!

I am still deciding what to do about Chris's suggestion about "splitting this into two structures" to allow for expressing the category of manifolds with a fixed model space. I think it is a worthwhile idea to explore, but will require a substantial refactor. The PR will have to grow a bit larger in size and it will diverge more significantly from TopCat--but those aren't necessarily bad things.

I will work on an alternative and see what I can come up with.

Making the right design decisions at the beginning is an art, and important! Nobody is going to object to PRs getting bigger and perhaps being split into smaller ones if ultimately it's the right decision.

It's much easier than having to refactor later!

For context, this is the proposed definition:

import Mathlib
open CategoryTheory
open scoped Manifold ContDiff

/-- The category of `C^n` 𝕜-manifolds. -/
structure MfldCat (𝕜 : Type v) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] (n : ℕ∞ω) where
  /-- The object in `MfldCat` associated to a type equipped with the appropriate typeclasses. -/
  of ::
  /-- The underlying type. -/
  carrier : Type u
  /-- The model normed space. -/
  E : Type u
  /-- The chart space. -/
  H : Type u
  [instNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [instNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [instTopologicalSpaceH : TopologicalSpace H]
  /-- The model with corners. -/
  I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H
  [instTopologicalSpace : TopologicalSpace carrier]
  [instChartedSpace : ChartedSpace H carrier]
  [instIsManifold : IsManifold I n carrier]

and here is my comment on github:

How about splitting this into two structures? The first one, let's call it ModelWithCorners.MfldCat, would have E, H and I as parameters. This would give a natural way to consider e.g. the category of manifolds of dimension n without boundary.

The second one would be equivalent to the one you currently have: It would take E, H and I as fields and a term of ModelWithCorners.MfldCat I.

Jack McCarthy said:

I will work on an alternative and see what I can come up with.

There is probably no need to do this (but might be a good exercise of course). In this case, I think the relevant people can give advice based on an implementation idea.

Aie, so we have a free universe metavariable? This always scares me. I think it means that any time you do not write MfldCat.{u} 𝕜 you run the risk of code becoming ridiculously slow because Lean is trying to solve for u and ploughing through gigantic terms with an inefficient algorithm before finally deciding "actually the solution is u ".

Kevin Buzzard said:

I think it means that any time you do not write MfldCat.{u} 𝕜 you run the risk of code becoming ridiculously slow because Lean is trying to solve for u and ploughing through gigantic terms with an inefficient algorithm before finally deciding "actually the solution is u ".

This is not avoidable though and also what we have for docs#TopCat, docs#RingCat etc. Indeed, we always tell people in review to explicitly specify the .{u}.

Kevin Buzzard said:

I don't think it's unreasonable to simply ask the community (e.g. in #mathlib4 ) whether this might be the case.

Good idea, I will make a thread about it.
And yes, I'm not sure if it possible to avoid the .{u} in this case. I will add it more explicitly in my code if there is a chance it will impact performance.

Well, I suspect that this is what we will want to do in the end. You make a strong case for it in your comments. But I'm happy to wait for more input first.

@Dagur Asgeirsson Thanks for the review! You helped shortened the PR by 60 lines by removing redundant API :tada: I left a few clarifying questions on a few of your comments for when you get around to them.

I do have one other question: Could you give an opinion on the "Separate substructure v.s. Subcategory" debate? Two of my reviewers are in disagreement about whether we should define a separate category of "Manifolds with a fixed model space," or if that should just be implemented as a subcategory of MfldCat. I need to resolve the discussion before I can move forward.
update-- Now that I got 4 reviewers (thanks again guys!) I removed the awaiting-author tag and requested a 2nd round of reviews on github. Hopefully we can get this PR finished up soon!

Not at a computer right now, but in general I’m team FullSubcategory these days. But there may be exceptions and I’ll look into the details after the weekend. Regarding your question on the PR about the ofHom section, don’t remove all of it, just what I specifically suggested for now
And regarding the TopCat lemma you asked about on the PR, I’ve already opened a PR removing it

It's good to hear your opinion on separate structures vs. FullSubcategory because we'll have to make that decision for the category of finite-dimensional (Hausdorff, boundaryless etc.) manifolds, but I think the question in the PR is more whether we need the suggested category at all: the category of all manifolds modelled on a specific model
I personally don't see why, but I'm also not strictly opposed to having it of course

Thanks Dagur, this is really helpful feedback. I just saw your TopCat PR, it looks good.

Personally, I can see a use case for the category of manifolds without boundary, since some theorems only hold in that setting. Also worth noting: the classical definition of "Manifold with Boundary" doesn't form a cartesian monoidal structure but the more general "Manifold with Corners" (my current implementation) does. There is granularity here that is worth studying.

I like your suggestion to define the specific models as a FullSubcategory. I personally feel that the "canonical" MfldCat should merely be a wrapper around IsManifold hypotheses. Additional requirements like FiniteDimensional E or T2Space M or Boundaryless I can implemented as a subcategory.

#38560 Now that the API for MfldCat is (seemingly) stable, I've decided to move forward with the next stage: endowing MfldCat with a Cartesian monoidal structure. This adds ~60 lines and closely mirrors the implementation of Algebra/Category/Grp/CartesianMonoidal.lean

@Michael Rothgang Sorry to ping you, but could you take a quick look at this when you get the chance? Chris and Dagur both opted to defer to your expertise regarding manifolds.

The question is about the category of manifolds with a specific model (i.e. Manifolds without boundary). Dagur supports my current implementation which would use FullSubcategory to construct such a category. Chris requests a separate category of ModelWithCorners distinct from MfldCat itself.
I'll try to take a look: note that I'm still travelling until end of next week, and will have virtually no time until then.
Thanks I really appreciate it

Per @Christian Merten's suggestion, I have opened a separate PR #41109 defining ModelWithCorners.MfldCat, the category of C^n manifolds modeled
on a fixed I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H.

I will now refactor the main PR to build on top of #41109.
